history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Nyay Mandir (lit. 'Temple of Justice') is a historic court building beside Sursagar Lake, opened on 30 November 1896 by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III and designed by Madras architect Robert Fellowes Chisholm in Indo-Saracenic style (Gothic, Renaissance and Mughal elements), built at Rs 7.44 lakh. It was originally built as 'The Maharani Chimnabai Market', named for Sayajirao's deceased first wife Chimnabai I, then used as a town hall, and converted into the imperial 'Maharani Chimnabai Nyay Mandir' law courts; after Baroda State's merger the last ruler Pratapsinhrao Gaekwad gave his last public speech from it. It housed the Vadodara district courts (central hall with mosaic tiles and a statue of Maharani Chimnabai). The CSV brief's label 'Sayaji Palace of Justice' is not a documented name for the building - flagged. CSV row is a civic-heritage record, not a temple.
